title: What are outliers and why are they dangerous?

cues.en: Mike: Now let's start talking about outliers.
cues.zh: Mike：現在開始談離群值。

cues.en: I'm sure you've heard this term before.
cues.zh: 我相信你以前聽過這個詞。

cues.en: I've certainly used it in this course.
cues.zh: 這門課中我也確實用過。

cues.en: I'm going to give you a better idea, a better sense of what outliers are, and I will introduce in this video some related terms like leverage.
cues.zh: 我要讓你更清楚地理解什麼是離群值，這部影片也會介紹一些相關術語，例如槓桿值。

cues.en: There are two primary strategies for dealing with outliers, and I will also give an overview of those two strategies.
cues.zh: 處理離群值主要有兩種策略，我也會概述這兩種策略。

cues.en: And I think most importantly, what I want to convey to you in this lecture is that the term outlier is a little bit ambiguous.
cues.zh: 我認為最重要的是，這堂課想傳達：離群值這個詞其實有點模糊。

cues.en: It's often difficult to know exactly which data points are outliers.
cues.zh: 往往很難確切知道，哪些資料點才是離群值。

cues.en: So first of all, an outlier is often given several different names.
cues.zh: 首先，離群值有好幾種不同名稱。

cues.en: So you might hear an outlier being called an anomaly or an extreme data value or a deviant data point.
cues.zh: 你可能會聽到它被稱為異常值、極端資料值，或偏離的資料點。

cues.en: Non-representative data, this is one of my favorite alternative terms for an outlier.
cues.zh: 不具代表性的資料，是我很喜歡的一種替代說法。

cues.en: And some people might call it noise.
cues.zh: 有些人也可能稱它為雜訊。

cues.en: It depends a little bit on the scenario and the discipline, but these are terms that you will often come across.
cues.zh: 要看情境和學科領域，但這些都是經常會遇到的詞。

cues.en: Okay, so here we have some data.
cues.zh: 好，這裡有一些資料。

cues.en: These are one-dimensional data.
cues.zh: 這是一維資料。

cues.en: This is really just values on the y-axis.
cues.zh: 實際上只是 Y 軸上的數值。

cues.en: The data points all have, like, these tiny, random x-axis offsets, but that's just to make sure that they're not all completely hidden so you can see the variation here.
cues.zh: 每個資料點都有很小的隨機 X 軸偏移，只是為了避免它們完全被遮住，讓你看得見變化。

cues.en: All right, so it's pretty obvious that this data point here is, call it what you want, an outlier, an anomaly, non-representative data.
cues.zh: 好，很明顯，這個資料點，不管你稱它為離群值、異常值，還是不具代表性的資料，

cues.en: This is clearly unusual.
cues.zh: 它顯然不尋常。

cues.en: This we can all agree is an outlier because it is really far away from the rest of the distribution.
cues.zh: 大家應該都同意，這是離群值，因為它距離其他分布真的很遠。

cues.en: So that case is pretty clear.
cues.zh: 這種情況很清楚。

cues.en: But now let's look at a situation like this.
cues.zh: 但現在看看這種情況。

cues.en: Here, you know, most of the data are clustered down here, and I don't know, what do you think?
cues.zh: 大部分資料都聚集在下面，你覺得呢？

cues.en: Are these outliers?
cues.zh: 這些是離群值嗎？

cues.en: Maybe this one is an outlier, or these two.
cues.zh: 也許這一個是，或這兩個是。

cues.en: What if we would call all five of these points an outlier?
cues.zh: 如果把這五個點都稱為離群值呢？

cues.en: So we put some threshold here.
cues.zh: 也就是在這裡設一個門檻。

cues.en: But then how about this point?
cues.zh: 但那這個點呢？

cues.en: It's also a little bit far away from the distribution.
cues.zh: 它距離分布也稍微遠了一點。

cues.en: Well, you're starting to get the idea.
cues.zh: 你開始理解問題了。

cues.en: There are cases where an outlier is really easy to identify, and there are other cases where it's not so clear whether there are outliers or how many outliers there are.
cues.zh: 有些情況下，離群值很容易辨識；另一些情況，則不太確定有沒有離群值，或究竟有幾個。

cues.en: So there is a little bit of ambiguity.
cues.zh: 所以有一點模糊性。

cues.en: So these are one-dimensional data.
cues.zh: 這些是一維資料。

cues.en: Things get more complicated when we have multi-dimensional data.
cues.zh: 資料是多維時，事情就更複雜了。

cues.en: So here is a data set with two dimensions.
cues.zh: 這裡是具有兩個維度的資料集。

cues.en: Imagine this is two features.
cues.zh: 想像這是兩個特徵。

cues.en: Maybe this dimension is like, I don't know, how often people eat at a Chinese restaurant in a given year, and this is how many times people eat at a pizzeria
cues.zh: 也許這個維度是人們一年中去中式餐廳吃飯的次數，而這個維度是去披薩店吃飯的次數，

cues.en: in a given year.
cues.zh: 同樣以一年計。

cues.en: So we have these two-dimensional data and now what do you call an outlier?
cues.zh: 現在有這些二維資料，該把什麼稱為離群值？

cues.en: So this data point here is certainly unusual.
cues.zh: 這個資料點確實不尋常。

cues.en: I don't know if it's an outlier or not, but it is unusually large on this dimension, on the y-axis.
cues.zh: 我不知道它算不算離群值，但在這個維度，也就是 Y 軸上，它異常地大。

cues.en: But when you project this down on the x-axis, this data point is actually not at all unusual on this x-axis.
cues.zh: 但把它投影到 X 軸後，這個資料點在 X 軸上其實完全不奇怪。

cues.en: Likewise here, you know, this is an extreme value on the x-axis, maybe not an outlier per se, but, you know, at least it still drives my point home
cues.zh: 同樣地，這裡是 X 軸上的極端值，也許不算真正的離群值，但至少仍能說明重點：

cues.en: that this data is unusually large for the x-axis, but it is actually pretty small on the y-axis.
cues.zh: 這個資料在 X 軸上異常地大，但在 Y 軸上其實相當小。

cues.en: So when you get to multidimensional data, it gets even more difficult, even more ambiguous, what exactly an outlier is and what you would call an outlier.
cues.zh: 所以到了多維資料，要確定什麼是離群值、該把什麼稱為離群值，會更加困難、更加模糊。

cues.en: So where do we get outliers? Where do they come from?
cues.zh: 那離群值從哪裡來？它們如何產生？

cues.en: Well, outliers can come from many different possible sources.
cues.zh: 離群值可能來自很多不同來源。

cues.en: Maybe you have noisy data, and that gives you outliers.
cues.zh: 也許資料有雜訊，因而出現離群值。

cues.en: Maybe you have noisy equipment, if your sensors don't really work so well, or, you know, whatever it is you're using to measure from the universe, measured nature,
cues.zh: 也許設備有雜訊，感測器運作不太好，或者你用來測量宇宙、測量自然界的設備，

cues.en: maybe your equipment is faulty, or it's a little bit noisy.
cues.zh: 可能有故障，或帶有一點雜訊。

cues.en: And there could be human error.
cues.zh: 也可能是人為錯誤。

cues.en: If you have people who, like, research assistants or secretaries who have to type in data, key in data, they could make an innocent typo, a little mistake,
cues.zh: 如果有人，例如研究助理或秘書，必須手動輸入資料，可能無意間打錯字，犯個小錯，

cues.en: and that could cause an outlier.
cues.zh: 就可能造成離群值。

cues.en: If you are testing human participants, you could get some non-cooperative research participants.
cues.zh: 如果測試對象是人，也可能遇到不配合的研究參與者。

cues.en: Maybe you're filling in a, you have a survey online, and people are filling in your survey, and then you get just some, I don't know why people are like this, but just, you know,
cues.zh: 也許你有一份線上問卷，大家正在填寫，然後出現一些人，我也不知道為什麼有人會這樣，

cues.en: someone who feels like screwing up your research, and they're gonna fill out the form in this really weird way and give you non-valid data.
cues.zh: 就是想搞砸你的研究，用很奇怪的方式填表，給你無效資料。

cues.en: Or outliers can also just come from natural variation.
cues.zh: 離群值也可能只是來自自然變異。

cues.en: There's a lot of variability in the world, particularly in biology and human behavior.
cues.zh: 世界上有很多變異，尤其是生物學和人類行為。

cues.en: So what might be an unusual or non-representative data point might actually still be valid.
cues.zh: 所以一個不尋常或不具代表性的資料點，其實仍可能是有效資料。

cues.en: You know, it's not because of noise.
cues.zh: 它不是來自雜訊。

cues.en: It's not because of human error.
cues.zh: 也不是來自人為錯誤。

cues.en: It's just some natural variation.
cues.zh: 只是自然變異。

cues.en: Okay, so that's a bit about outliers and other terms for outliers.
cues.zh: 好，這是關於離群值，以及離群值其他名稱的一些介紹。

cues.en: I wanna talk about why outliers are bad.
cues.zh: 接著談為什麼離群值不好。

cues.en: Why do we have to worry about outliers in the data?
cues.zh: 為什麼需要擔心資料中的離群值？

cues.en: Well, the thing is that many statistical analyses use squared terms to run the analyses.
cues.zh: 因為很多統計分析在執行時會使用平方項。

cues.en: And this is just a small subset of the types of statistical analyses that at some point in the analysis will square terms.
cues.zh: 這裡只列出一小部分，會在分析過程某個環節將項目平方的統計分析類型。

cues.en: Now, why is that bad when you square terms?
cues.zh: 為什麼平方會有問題？

cues.en: Well, when you already have large data points that are outliers, when you square them, they become huge.
cues.zh: 本來就很大的離群資料點，平方後會變得巨大。

cues.en: That's the whole thing about squaring, that large values become really, really large.
cues.zh: 平方的特性就是，大數值會變得非常非常大。

cues.en: Here you see an example.
cues.zh: 這裡可以看到一個例子。

cues.en: These are some data that I generated, and then I artificially implanted one outlier over here.
cues.zh: 這些是我產生的資料，然後在這裡人工加入一個離群值。

cues.en: And here, this is exactly the same data.
cues.zh: 這裡則是完全相同的資料。

cues.en: All I did was square it.
cues.zh: 唯一做的就是平方。

cues.en: This tick mark, by the way, is one.
cues.zh: 順帶一提，這個刻度是 1。

cues.en: That's why these values get smaller.
cues.zh: 所以這些數值會變小。

cues.en: Because, you know, when you square a number between zero and one, it gets smaller.
cues.zh: 因為 0 和 1 之間的數字平方後會變小。

cues.en: So these values get smaller every.
cues.zh: 所以這些數值都會變小。

cues.en: All the numbers above one get bigger, so that's fine.
cues.zh: 所有大於 1 的數字都會變大，這沒問題。

cues.en: But look how much bigger, relatively bigger, the outlier gets compared to its distribution here when squared versus here.
cues.zh: 但比較這裡和平方後的這裡，看看離群值相對於其分布，變大了多少。

cues.en: So this is only a kind of bad outlier here.
cues.zh: 這裡還只是有點糟糕的離群值。

cues.en: And here, it's horrible. It's huge.
cues.zh: 到這裡就非常糟，變得巨大。

cues.en: It's really, really far away.
cues.zh: 距離真的非常非常遠。

cues.en: So you can have results of analyses like correlations, regressions, ANOVA, general linear models, these results can be incorrect.
cues.zh: 因此，相關、迴歸、ANOVA、一般線性模型等分析的結果，可能會不正確。

cues.en: They can be skewed because of one single data point.
cues.zh: 單一資料點就可能讓它們偏斜。

cues.en: you'll get to see some examples of this in code.
cues.zh: 之後會透過程式看到一些例子。

cues.en: Okay, another feature, which I will also show you, illustrate to you in an image in a few slides, is that outliers can have more impact on these statistical results when the sample size is small.
cues.zh: 另一個特性，再過幾張投影片也會用圖片說明，就是樣本數小時，離群值對統計結果的影響可能更大。

cues.en: So you should always be concerned about outliers, but if you have a small data set, then you need to be even more concerned about outliers.
cues.zh: 因此，始終應該留意離群值，但如果資料集很小，就必須更加留意。

cues.en: Okay, so another concept when dealing with outliers is that not all outliers are created equal.
cues.zh: 好，處理離群值的另一個概念是，並非所有離群值都一樣。

cues.en: Some outliers are more deleterious to your statistical results, and other outliers are less influential on the final results.
cues.zh: 有些對統計結果的傷害較大，有些對最終結果的影響較小。

cues.en: And that has to do with where the outliers are positioned in different dimensions of the data.
cues.zh: 這和離群值位於資料不同維度上的位置有關。

cues.en: So here you see an example.
cues.zh: 這裡有個例子。

cues.en: Here I have some data points.
cues.zh: 這裡有一些資料點。

cues.en: I think this is, what is this?
cues.zh: 我想這是……有幾個？

cues.en: 10 data points here, and then one outlier here.
cues.zh: 這裡有 10 個資料點，這裡還有一個離群值。

cues.en: So this is also an interesting case because you can see that this is not an outlier on the x dimension.
cues.zh: 這也是很有趣的情況，因為可以看到它在 X 維度上不是離群值。

cues.en: It's only an outlier on the y dimension.
cues.zh: 只有在 Y 維度上是離群值。

cues.en: Now, if you would compute a best fit line, with and without the outlier, so that would look something like this, this best fit line, you'll learn more about,
cues.zh: 如果分別在包含和不包含離群值的情況下，計算最佳擬合直線，會得到像這樣的圖；關於這條最佳擬合直線，

cues.en: if, you know, this seems a little mysterious, you'll learn more about this on the section on regression.
cues.zh: 如果現在覺得有點神祕，之後在迴歸那一章會學到更多。

cues.en: But essentially, we're just drawing a single line through the data that kind of best fits the relationship or best describes the relationship between x and y.
cues.zh: 基本上，就是在資料中畫一條最能擬合，或最能描述 X 和 Y 之間關係的直線。

cues.en: So the blue line shows the best fit line excluding this outlier.
cues.zh: 藍線是不包含離群值時的最佳擬合直線。

cues.en: And the yellow line is including this outlier.
cues.zh: 黃線則包含這個離群值。

cues.en: Now, the reason why this data point here has low leverage is because it has relatively little influence on the slope of the line.
cues.zh: 這個資料點的槓桿值低，是因為它對直線斜率的影響相對小。

cues.en: You can see that the slope of the line doesn't really change.
cues.zh: 可以看到，直線斜率並沒有真正改變。

cues.en: The intercept is changing, so there's this kind of shift on the y-axis.
cues.zh: 截距改變了，所以在 Y 軸上出現這種平移。

cues.en: But the slope is basically the same with and without this outlier.
cues.zh: 但有沒有這個離群值，斜率基本上都相同。

cues.en: So this outlier has low leverage.
cues.zh: 所以這個離群值的槓桿值低。

cues.en: It has a relatively small impact on the result.
cues.zh: 它對結果的影響相對小。

cues.en: And that's because, you know, with regression, usually we're not so interested in the intercept, this y-axis shift.
cues.zh: 因為在迴歸中，通常我們不太在意截距，也就是這個 Y 軸平移。

cues.en: Usually, we're interested in the slope, the relationship between x and y.
cues.zh: 通常在意的是斜率，也就是 X 和 Y 的關係。

cues.en: Okay, and what I did over here was take another example, so still 10 data points here, and then I put in an outlier here.
cues.zh: 這裡則是另一個例子，一樣有 10 個資料點，再在這裡加入一個離群值。

cues.en: Now, this outlier has higher leverage, and the effect of that is that it really affects the slope.
cues.zh: 這個離群值的槓桿值比較高，會真正影響斜率。

cues.en: It's really pulling up the slope of this line here.
cues.zh: 它明顯把這條線的斜率向上拉。

cues.en: So you can see, you know, comparing the effect of the outlier on the slope here versus here, this outlier is much worse compared to this outlier.
cues.zh: 比較這裡和這裡，離群值對斜率的影響，就會看到這個比另一個糟得多。

cues.en: So this is an example with 11 data points in total.
cues.zh: 這個例子總共有 11 個資料點。

cues.en: And then what I did here was take the same relationship between x and y, and I just generated, I think this was a hundred points, looks like it could be a hundred data points.
cues.zh: 這裡則保留相同的 X、Y 關係，只是產生了，我想是 100 個點，看起來可能有 100 個資料點。

cues.en: And now you see that this outlier still has high leverage, but the effect on the slope isn't as bad as it is here with the small data set.
cues.zh: 現在可以看到，這個離群值的槓桿值仍然高，但對斜率的影響，沒有小資料集這裡那麼嚴重。

cues.en: So a small data set, the outlier can have a really big effect on the statistical results.
cues.zh: 所以資料集很小時，離群值可能對統計結果造成很大的影響。

cues.en: And here, when you have a larger data set, you're still going to have a negative impact from the outlier, but it's not as bad.
cues.zh: 而資料集比較大時，離群值仍會造成負面影響，但沒那麼糟。

cues.en: Okay, so what do you do about outliers?
cues.zh: 好，那該怎麼處理離群值？

cues.en: How do you deal with outliers?
cues.zh: 如何應對它們？

cues.en: In general, there are two families of approaches, two general strategies for dealing with outliers in your data.
cues.zh: 一般而言，處理資料中離群值的方法，可分成兩大類、兩種一般策略。

cues.en: One strategy is to identify outliers and remove them from the data before you run any analyses.
cues.zh: 一種策略是，在執行任何分析之前，先辨識出離群值並將其移除。

cues.en: So you go through. You clean your data.
cues.zh: 也就是逐一檢視，清理資料。

cues.en: You inspect your data.
cues.zh: 檢查資料。

cues.en: I will show you, over the next several videos, multiple ways for identifying outliers.
cues.zh: 接下來幾部影片，會介紹好幾種辨識離群值的方法。

cues.en: But the assumption is that outliers are junk.
cues.zh: 但這裡的假設是，離群值沒有用。

cues.en: They are garbage. They are noise.
cues.zh: 它們是垃圾、是雜訊。

cues.en: They are not valid.
cues.zh: 它們無效。

cues.en: They are not contributing any useful information to the data set, and therefore it is justified to remove them.
cues.zh: 不會對資料集提供任何有用資訊，因此有理由移除。

cues.en: Now, that is an assumption.
cues.zh: 這是一個假設。

cues.en: You as the researcher, you as the the data scientist, you have to decide whether that assumption is valid.
cues.zh: 身為研究者、資料科學家，你必須決定這個假設是否成立。

cues.en: So that's strategy 1.
cues.zh: 這就是第一種策略。

cues.en: Strategy 2 is to leave the outliers in the data.
cues.zh: 第二種策略，是把離群值留在資料裡。

cues.en: So you don't remove the outliers.
cues.zh: 也就是不移除離群值。

cues.en: You leave them in the data.
cues.zh: 讓它們留在資料中。

cues.en: But you know that the outliers can have negative impacts on the results.
cues.zh: 但你知道它們可能對結果造成負面影響。

cues.en: So you use different kinds of statistical analyses.
cues.zh: 因此改用不同種類的統計分析。

cues.en: You use robust methods that will attenuate or completely eliminate the impact of outliers on the results.
cues.zh: 使用穩健方法，減弱甚至完全消除離群值對結果的影響。

cues.en: And there are several robust methods that are, so statistical analysis methods that are robust to outliers.
cues.zh: 有好幾種穩健方法，也就是不易受離群值影響的統計分析方法。

cues.en: You will learn them later on in specific sections.
cues.zh: 之後在特定章節會學到。

cues.en: But, you know, there's nonparametric t-tests.
cues.zh: 例如無母數 t 檢定。

cues.en: There's Spearman correlations. There's permutation testing.
cues.zh: 還有 Spearman 相關、置換檢定。

cues.en: There is robust weighted regression and iteratively re-weighted regression.
cues.zh: 以及穩健加權迴歸、迭代重新加權迴歸。

cues.en: So there's several techniques that you can use where you don't actually have to remove the outliers.
cues.zh: 所以有好幾種技術，可以讓你不必實際移除離群值。

cues.en: You can keep them in the data, and you apply specific analysis methods that reduce the impact of those outliers on the results.
cues.zh: 可以把它們留在資料中，套用特定分析方法，降低它們對結果的影響。

cues.en: So this strategy is based on the assumption that the outliers may be unusual.
cues.zh: 這種策略的假設是，離群值也許不尋常。

cues.en: They're a little bit different.
cues.zh: 它們稍微不同。

cues.en: Maybe they are non-representative, but they are still valid data.
cues.zh: 也許不具代表性，但仍然是有效資料。

cues.en: They are important data, and you don't want to remove them, because it's not justified to remove them.
cues.zh: 它們是重要資料，不應移除，因為沒有充分理由移除。

cues.en: Because they are real genuine data points, even if they are a little bit unusual.
cues.zh: 因為它們是真實的資料點，即使有一點不尋常。

cues.en: So I can teach you these different strategies, removing outliers and leaving outliers in and using robust methods.
cues.zh: 所以我可以教你這些不同策略，包括移除離群值，或保留離群值並使用穩健方法。

cues.en: But it's up to you to decide which approach is appropriate for your particular data set.
cues.zh: 但哪種方式適合你的特定資料集，必須由你決定。

cues.en: I cannot tell you which assumption is valid.
cues.zh: 我無法告訴你哪個假設才成立。

cues.en: But you can see these assumptions are quite different.
cues.zh: 但可以看到，這些假設相當不同。

cues.en: These are, in fact, polar opposites of each other.
cues.zh: 事實上，它們完全相反。

cues.en: So you will have to make that determination.
cues.zh: 因此必須由你做出判斷。

cues.en: So the conclusions here are that outliers must be investigated and evaluated.
cues.zh: 這裡的結論是，必須調查並評估離群值。

cues.en: You should always approach your data with the assumption that there could be outliers in there.
cues.zh: 面對資料時，始終應該假設其中可能有離群值。

cues.en: Never assume that your data are perfectly clean and, you know, without any outliers whatsoever.
cues.zh: 絕對不要假設資料完美乾淨、完全沒有任何離群值。

cues.en: So you always have to be careful and meticulous and thoughtful to look through your data in case there are outliers.
cues.zh: 因此，總是必須仔細、謹慎、有所思考地檢視資料，確認是否有離群值。

cues.en: And secondly, you should never just remove outliers without thinking about it.
cues.zh: 第二，不應不加思考就直接移除離群值。

cues.en: Now, it's not to say that you should never remove outliers, definitely there is a place for removing outliers, but do it with some thought, and think carefully
cues.zh: 這不是說永遠不能移除，移除離群值確實有其適用情境，但要經過思考，仔細想想

cues.en: about why you are removing those outliers, and whether it's justified to remove those outliers.
cues.zh: 為什麼要移除，以及是否有充分理由。

cues.en: Okay, and then the third point here is never just ignore outliers.
cues.zh: 第三點，絕對不要直接忽略離群值。

cues.en: I guess that's kind of redundant with these first two points.
cues.zh: 我想這和前兩點有些重複。

cues.en: Although, I think what I mean here is that outliers can be very informative about the kind of experiment that you're running about the nature of the equipment
cues.zh: 不過，我這裡想表達的應該是，離群值可能透露很多資訊，讓你了解實驗的類型、設備的性質，

cues.en: and the nature of the data that you're gathering.
cues.zh: 以及所收集資料的性質。

cues.en: And so looking carefully at these outliers and determining where outliers come from and why they are present in your data might actually be really important to understanding
cues.zh: 所以仔細檢視離群值，判斷它們從哪裡來、為什麼出現在資料中，對理解情況可能非常重要。

cues.en: maybe there's something wrong with the experiment, there's something weird with the data acquisition system, and I think that's probably why I wrote here, "Why outliers just might be
cues.zh: 也許實驗有問題，或者資料擷取系統有奇怪之處。我想這就是為什麼寫下：「離群值為何可能是

cues.en: the most important part of your research."
cues.zh: 你研究中最重要的部分。」

cues.en: So just, when there are unusual things happening in the data, don't dismiss them.
cues.zh: 所以，資料中發生不尋常的事時，不要直接忽視。

cues.en: You should investigate them and think carefully about them.
cues.zh: 應該調查，仔細思考。
